talks.title: No Server, No Cry: the Ups and Downs of Building a Scalable Security Serverless Platform
talks.teaser: Lessons from building a scalable security platform on serverless cloud infrastructure.
talks.summary:
An engineering lead from Jit delivers a guide to architecting secure, production-ready serverless applications in the Cloud Village, addressing the misconceptions surrounding serverless security [00:00]. While cloud providers manage underlying physical infrastructure and OS patching, the speaker clarifies that tenants remain entirely responsible for identity, access controls, code vulnerabilities, secrets management, and runtime logging under the shared responsibility model [02:33].

The presentation maps the OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities directly onto serverless architectures, detailing mitigations for broken access controls, command injection, and vulnerable third-party dependencies [03:03, 05:31]. The speaker demonstrates automated enforcement strategies, including deploying AWS IAM Access Analyzer to restrict overly permissive Lambda execution roles down to least-privilege policies [08:05, 10:52], configuring Amazon CloudWatch metric alarms to detect anomalous DynamoDB scans [11:16], using open-source tools like Prowler and Checkov for infrastructure-as-code linting [13:36, 14:10], and running Google OSV Scanner to detect outdated dependencies and unmaintained Lambda runtime environments [16:41, 17:33].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Transforming Identity Protection: Innovating with AI and Attack Paths
talks.teaser: Combining AI and attack-path analysis to transform cloud identity protection.
talks.summary:
In this insightful presentation from the DEF CON 33 Cloud Village, speaker Filipas addresses the escalating challenges of securing machine identities across modern multi-cloud architectures. Opening at 00:00, Filipas outlines how rapid cloud adoption has resulted in non-human identities vastly outnumbering human users, creating complex and fragmented security boundaries.

At 03:00, he examines the fundamental anatomy of machine identities—including IAM service accounts, API tokens, IAM roles, and automated workload credentials across AWS, GCP, and Azure. At 05:01, he analyzes common misconfigurations in cloud trust policies, showing how over-permissive role assumptions and privilege sprawling enable attackers to execute lateral movement.

He demonstrates attack path modeling at 12:00, illustrating how graph analysis can map hidden identity relationships and privilege escalation vectors. He concludes at 18:00 by advocating for continuous entitlement auditing, least-privilege automation, and AI-driven path disruption to isolate and protect critical cloud infrastructure. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: No IP, No Problem: Exfiltrating Data Behind IAP
talks.teaser: Exfiltrating cloud data from behind Google Identity-Aware Proxy without a public IP.
talks.summary:
A cloud security researcher demonstrates how Google Cloud Platform's Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) can be covertly abused to exfiltrate sensitive data from internal applications without requiring public IP assignments or external network access [00:00]. The talk begins with an architectural breakdown of GCP IAP, explaining how the proxy acts as a centralized perimeter that verifies user identities, enforces IAM policies, and injects authenticated identity tokens into requests forwarded to backend App Engine, Compute Engine, or GKE workloads [01:15, 02:11].

The researcher details a vulnerability stemming from cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) handling, where unauthenticated HTTP OPTIONS preflight requests are permitted through IAP by design to allow browser preflight negotiations [08:56, 09:06]. By gaining access to application configuration files (such as app.yaml) via CI/CD pipelines or internal App Engine deployment roles, an insider or compromised account can dynamically embed internal secrets into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header [13:26, 13:48]. An external attacker can then issue unauthenticated OPTIONS requests to harvest the reflected secrets from outside the protected network [11:26]. The session concludes with detection strategies using Cloud Audit Logs to identify rapid bursts of App Engine createVersion API events [15:42] and recommendations for hardening deployment pipelines.

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Hypervisor Hangover: Persistence Mechanisms on ESXi - JC(Crashwire) and Nathan
talks.teaser: Novel ESXi hypervisor persistence techniques for maintaining long-term access in cloud environments.
talks.summary:
In this in-depth post-exploitation talk from the DEF CON 33 Cloud Village, researchers Nathan and JC (Crashwire) explore stealthy persistence mechanisms targeting VMware ESXi hypervisors. Beginning at 00:00, the speakers explain that hypervisors represent high-value enterprise targets that often suffer from a lack of defensive visibility and security monitoring compared to guest operating systems.

At 02:01, they break down hypervisor exploitation vectors, focusing on how attackers deploy malicious vSphere Installation Bundles (VIBs) to survive system reboots and execute arbitrary code. At 05:00, they dissect real-world malware campaigns—specifically analyzing Python-based C2 backdoors such as "VirtualPita" and "VirtualPie" that manipulate ESXi configuration files to maintain stealthy access.

Moving to defensive operations at 18:00, the presenters examine how attackers attempt to bypass secure boot and code signature enforcement. Concluding at 25:00, they provide actionable hardening guidance: strictly isolating ESXi management interfaces, enforcing signed VIB verification, monitoring host profile compliance, and forwarding tamper-resistant hypervisor syslog telemetry to central SIEM platforms. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Weaponizing SageMaker AI: Real-World Offense in Machine Learning Platforms
talks.teaser: Exploiting AWS SageMaker to gain persistence and exfiltrate data from ML platforms.
talks.summary:
A cloud security researcher explores offensive tradecraft targeting machine learning infrastructure in the Cloud Village, focusing on Amazon SageMaker deployment flaws [00:05]. The talk examines how default "easy button" configurations and quick-start templates provision overly permissive IAM service roles behind convenient interfaces [03:53].

The presentation demonstrates step-by-step attack techniques executed from within compromised Jupyter notebook instances, including abusing wildcard permissions (`secretsmanager:ListSecrets`) to enumerate organizational secrets across the entire AWS account [07:44]. The researcher shows how attackers can map underlying Glue Data Catalogs and Athena table metadata to harvest sensitive training datasets [11:51], exploit subtle authorization boundaries between Amazon Cognito application identities and AWS IAM roles [15:56], and script automated enumeration routines to discover exploitable cloud privilege escalation paths [20:20].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Restless Guests: From Subscription to Backdoor Intruder
talks.teaser: Turning Azure subscription access into persistent backdoor access across tenants.
talks.summary:
In this eye-opening case study from the DEF CON 33 Cloud Village, a cloud security researcher uncovers an unexpected privilege escalation vector involving external guest accounts in Microsoft Azure. Opening at 00:02, the speaker shares the real-world investigation that inspired the research: discovering how an unprivileged external partner guest user successfully created a new Azure subscription within a client tenant.

At 04:03, the talk dissects Azure Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) identity structures, subscription hierarchies, and default permission scopes. At 14:00, the speaker demonstrates how external guest accounts can exploit loose default tenant settings to enumerate organizational directories, inspect existing service principals, and provision rogue cloud subscriptions that serve as covert persistence backdoors.

At 22:00, the presenter explores the lateral movement and data exfiltration implications of unauthorized subscription creation. The session wraps up at 28:00 with concrete hardening recommendations: reconfiguring Entra ID external collaboration settings to restrict guest permissions, implementing strict subscription creation governance, and deploying Azure Monitor alert rules to flag anomalous tenant registrations. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: TencentGoat: An Intentionally Vulnerable Tencent Cloud Environment
talks.teaser: TencentGoat: an intentionally vulnerable Tencent Cloud environment for hands-on cloud security training.
talks.summary:
DevSecOps engineer Muhammad Yuga Nugraha introduces TencentGoat, an open-source, intentionally vulnerable playground designed to teach practical attack and defense techniques across Tencent Cloud environments [00:20]. Nugraha maps Tencent Cloud services to equivalent architectures in AWS and GCP, contrasting Cloud Virtual Machine (CVM), Cloud Object Storage (COS), and Cloud Access Management (CAM) with EC2, S3, and IAM [07:27].

The session walks through realistic misconfigurations and attack scenarios within the vulnerable environment, demonstrating how Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities in hosted web applications can be exploited to query the internal CVM Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) and extract temporary CAM credentials [11:05]. Nugraha compares Tencent's metadata architecture with AWS IMDSv2 token-based protections [14:53] and demonstrates how harvested service role credentials can be leveraged to escalate privileges across the tenant environment [18:35], providing remediation recommendations for cloud security teams.

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Building the Cross-Cloud Kill Chain: A DE's Playbook for AWS, Azure & GCP Detections
talks.teaser: Building cross-cloud kill chain detections for AWS, Azure, and GCP attacks.
talks.summary:
In this technical briefing from the DEF CON 33 Cloud Village, a detection engineer presents a practical operational playbook for building unified attack detection across AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform. Opening at 00:00, the speaker highlights the complexity detection teams face when monitoring disjointed log schemas across multiple cloud providers.

At 05:01, the session details log normalization strategies, demonstrating how to ingest and standardize AWS CloudTrail, GCP Cloud Audit Logs, and Azure Activity Logs into a cohesive monitoring framework. At 10:01, the presenter examines cross-cloud lateral movement techniques, showing how threat actors exploit federated IAM trust relationships, compromised CI/CD pipeline secrets, and shared Terraform state files to pivot between different cloud environments.

At 15:02, the talk focuses on identity enrichment, transforming raw user IDs and role ARNs into actionable operational context to cut alert fatigue. At 20:03, the speaker showcases practical Kusto Query Language (KQL) detection rules designed to catch credential access and unauthorized cross-cloud API interactions, concluding at 25:01 with strategies for automated SOC incident response. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Spotter - Universal Kubernetes Security Engine
talks.teaser: Spotter: a universal Kubernetes security engine for automated runtime threat detection.
talks.summary:
A Kubernetes security engineer presents Spotter, an open-source security engine designed to detect vulnerabilities and misconfigurations across modern container platforms [00:02]. The speaker analyzes the multi-layered attack surface of Kubernetes, explaining how risks emerge across decoupled tiers including container supply chains, deployment manifests, and runtime infrastructure [03:56].

The talk details Spotter's architecture, which includes over 140 built-in security rules evaluating platform and runtime controls [07:53]. The speaker demonstrates how Spotter categorizes and prioritizes risks by resource type and severity—focusing scrutiny on high-value targets like Pods, Deployments, and Kubernetes Secrets [11:46]—while integrating continuous scanning routines that synchronize with organizational risk registries during cluster releases [15:42]. The session concludes with a demonstration of mutating admission webhooks, illustrating how Spotter can automatically intercept deployment manifests requesting public Docker Hub images and reroute them to hardened internal private registries [19:30].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Quickstart for a Breach! When Official Installations Expose Your K8 and Your Cloud
talks.teaser: How official cloud installation scripts expose Kubernetes clusters and cloud environments to breach.
talks.summary:
In this pragmatic session from the DEF CON 33 Cloud Village, researchers Yosuman and Michael K. expose common security vulnerabilities introduced by official Kubernetes "quickstart" installation guides and Helm charts. Opening at 00:00, the speakers explain how vendor deployment templates often prioritize ease-of-use over security, leaving production clusters inadvertently exposed.

At 05:00, the presenters demonstrate how default NodePort and LoadBalancer configurations routinely expose internal services directly to the public internet without operator awareness. At 10:00, they present case studies on widely adopted open-source packages—including Apache Pinot and Meshery—showing that official default configurations frequently deploy administrative dashboards with blank or hardcoded credentials.

At 15:00, the speakers demonstrate cluster compromise, showing how exposed services allow attackers to extract service account tokens and move laterally across pods. Concluding at 20:00, they outline critical defensive practices: auditing third-party Helm charts prior to deployment, enforcing Kubernetes network policies to isolate pod traffic, and implementing automated ingress scanning to eliminate unintended public exposure. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Cognito, Ergo Some Extra Permissions
talks.teaser: Exploiting AWS Cognito misconfigurations to achieve privilege escalation and account takeover.
talks.summary:
Leo Tsaousis, Senior Security Consultant at WithSecure, analyzes a critical cloud security vulnerability in Amazon Cognito that allowed unauthenticated attackers to gain unauthorized permissions into AWS accounts through publicly shared CloudWatch dashboards [00:06]. Tsaousis recounts discovering that public dashboard URLs exposed underlying Amazon Cognito identity pools, creating an unauthenticated entry point into target environments prior to AWS's July 2024 patch [04:17].

The presentation breaks down the four-step exploitation chain, showing how reverse-engineering an undocumented viewer application revealed that identity pools configured with the legacy "Allow Classic Flow" setting allowed unauthenticated callers to exchange identity IDs directly for temporary AWS STS credentials [08:35, 17:33]. Tsaousis demonstrates how unauthenticated actors could invoke unauthorized AWS APIs—such as enumerating EC2 instance tags and infrastructure metadata—solely by knowing a dashboard URL [13:00]. The talk concludes by examining AWS's service-level remediation, identifying lingering post-patch configuration hazards, and offering guidance for auditing identity pools [22:00, 26:21].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Braving the Storm-2372: The Tempest Decoded
talks.teaser: Decoding the Storm-2372 threat actor campaign targeting cloud and identity infrastructure.
talks.summary:
In this detailed threat intelligence briefing from the DEF CON 33 Cloud Village, a researcher decodes the tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) of Storm-2372, an adversary specializing in sophisticated OAuth token abuse. Opening at 00:00, the speaker introduces device code phishing campaigns designed to circumvent modern multi-factor authentication (MFA) protections.

At 06:01, the presentation breaks down the mechanics of the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (Device Code Flow), explaining how attackers trick users into entering a one-time code on a legitimate identity portal. At 12:01, the speaker analyzes why these attacks succeed, showing that once a victim authenticates, the adversary receives a valid OAuth primary refresh token that grants persistent cloud access without triggering standard MFA re-prompts.

At 18:00, the talk evaluates detection engineering challenges, comparing user-agent, IP geolocation, and timestamp discrepancies between code generation and token redemption. Concluding at 24:00, the speaker outlines defensive mitigations: disabling device code flow across corporate tenants where not explicitly required, enforcing strict Conditional Access policies, and continuously monitoring for anomalous token issuance. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)
